correctness.rationale: For arbitrary individual conductances, the tree effective resistance is the sum of reciprocal weights along unique paths. Rescale maximum resistance to one and minimize strictly convex Σprice_e/ρ_e on path-sum constraints. A minimizer exists with positive coordinates and is unique, hence symmetry under leaf permutations is deduced, not assumed. All candidate diametral paths reduce to 2x,2y,x+y+z; z>0 forces x+y+z=1. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz yields the interior solution when √(pa) and √(qb) lie within one bridge root, while KKT gives left/right x=1/2 or y=1/2 cap regimes and the stated F. Boundaries are covered; budget scaling gives conductances B/(Fx),B/(Fy),B/(Fz), minimum F/B and uniqueness. The asymptotic equal-weight/optimal ratio→3/2 follows algebraically for fixed q, p→∞. Independent radical/budget branch tests checked both cap and triangle boundaries; finite sampling is no universal certificate.

originality.rationale: The general minimax effective-resistance problem, convex viewpoint and tree resistance identity are already known and not new. The identified contribution is the sharp globally optimal price-triangle active-set solution for independently adjustable double-star edges, including diametral pair classification. Older tree-diameter edge-reduction literature is plausible but may use a different linear reduction-price objective; its full statement remains a material priority risk.

value.rationale: This solves a natural robust network design problem on the two-hub tree family, exhibiting three competing path classes and a sharp priced transition. The exact unique allocation and fixed 3/2 performance ratio over equal conductances have a motivated optimization interpretation, beyond the general generic convex-program specification.

limitations: Numerical checks cannot establish global infinite-domain optimization; prior tree-upgrading literature has an access-limited comparison.
